title: Technology Clusters and National Power: The Case of Albany NanoTech

Semiconductor leadership increasingly depends on the strength of technology clusters that bring together advanced research infrastructure, industry, universities, skilled workers, and public investment. This report examines the Albany NanoTech Complex as a case study of how these assets can be organized into a durable strategic capability. Over more than 25 years, Albany has developed into a major public-private platform for leading-edge semiconductor research and development, prototyping, workforce development, and commercialization.Today, Albany supports research in sub-2-nanometer semiconductor technologies, advanced packaging, photonics, and quantum systems, while connecting U.S. capabilities with partners including IBM, Rapidus, imec, and Tokyo Electron. The report argues that Albany’s experience offers broader lessons for U.S. technology policy: Strategic clusters require sustained investment, effective institutions, shared infrastructure, industry partnerships, and workforce pipelines capable of translating research into manufacturing and national capability.
